USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold the tariff pressure already in place ($34B List 1 effective July 6, List 2 pending) and the $200B List 3 as a live threat, but do NOT fire the $200B trigger now. Instead open and press a negotiated channel with Beijing to convert our existing leverage into concrete concessions (market access, IP/tech-transfer commitments), letting the public-comment and hearing process run while signaling a credible path to de-escalation before the November midterms.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is mild-negative because the US holds the strong hand: we initiated on our chosen terrain, run a large goods-trade deficit with China, and the domestic economy shows no material damage yet — the broad dollar is up 5.4% YTD, industrial production is rising, consumer sentiment is ~98 (near cycle highs), and 10Y sits at 2.94% (country_health). China has matched our $34B tariffs dollar-for-dollar (timeline 2018-07-06), so the next rung ($200B, timeline 2018-07-10) would hit US consumers and supply chains just as the farm belt is already hurting — the July 24 USDA $12B farm bailout (soybeans ~-20%, corn/pork down ~15%; bipartisan 'welfare' criticism) is an admission of self-inflicted damage, and USTR hearings are pulling heavy business opposition to the new lists. That rising domestic and electoral cost, plus Beijing tolerating a 6-10% yuan slide, argues against gratuitous escalation. The action stance (mild de-escalation tilt, ~0) reflects that we should consolidate leverage and negotiate rather than escalate further on autopilot, keeping the $200B list as a credible stick while extracting concessions — a high threat score is not warranted here precisely because escalation is self-limiting and our economy can absorb the current tariff level.
key_factors: US holds asymmetric leverage (large goods-trade deficit with China, China depends on US market)
US macro strong: dollar +5.4% YTD, IP rising, consumer sentiment ~98, 10Y 2.94% — no material GDP drag yet
China matched $34B tariffs dollar-for-dollar on July 6; escalation invites symmetric retaliation
July 24 $12B USDA farm bailout signals real cost to politically key farm states (soybeans ~-20%)
$200B List 3 in comment/hearing phase with heavy business opposition — value as threat, not to fire now
Midterm elections (Nov) make uncontrolled escalation politically risky
China tolerating 6-10% yuan depreciation partially offsets tariffs for exporters

sources_cited.excerpt: USTR final two-stage $50B tariff plan: 25% on List 1 (~$34B, effective July 6) and List 2 (~$16B); China announces matching retaliation same day
List 1 tariffs take effect: US 25% on ~$34B of Chinese goods. China imposes matching ~$34B retaliation
USTR publishes proposed List 3: ~$200B of Chinese imports for an additional 10% tariff (~6,000 lines); public comment/hearing begins
Trump directs USTR to identify an additional ~$200B of Chinese imports for 10% tariffs if China retaliates
US-China joint statement; trade war 'on hold'; markets rally
White House announces US will proceed with Section 301 actions (25% on ~$50B); truce collapses
Broad dollar index up ~5.4% since Jan (107→112.9); USD strength offsets import-cost drag
US Industrial Production rising 101.7→103.4 (2018); economy expanding
USDA announces up to $12B emergency farm relief; soybean prices ~-20% since April; 'welfare for farmers' criticism
USTR public hearings Jul 24-25 (List 2) and Aug 20-23 (List 3, $200B) on proposed Section 301 tariffs
Trump trade war sinks yuan most since 2015 devaluation; Beijing says $200B threat 'totally unacceptable'
